passage: In the villages one anthropologist studied, a family that received a pig at a wedding was not expected to repay it soon, and no one ever named its price. Yet elders could recite, decades later, exactly who had given what to whom, and a gift left unreturned for too long became the subject of quiet gossip until a fitting gift went back. The absence of prices, she concluded, did not mean an absence of ______.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Elders remembered every gift for decades and gossiped about any left unreturned until a return gift settled it, so receivers clearly owed something even though no price was ever named: the absence of prices did not mean an absence of "indebtedness." "Gain" fails because each gift was eventually answered by a fitting one, so the system balanced obligations rather than letting anyone come out ahead. "Insolvency" fails because the gift eventually went back; no one is described as unable to repay. "Haggling" fails because no one ever named a price to bargain over.

deletion_test.kept_sentence: The absence of prices, she concluded, did not mean an absence of ______.
deletion_test.why: anything a reader links with prices and money (owing, profit, bargaining, inability to pay) can fill the sentence alone; only the remembered gifts and the gossip until a return show that what persisted was owing
